Dynamic epsilon is a method for preventing self-intersection artifacts in secondary rays (e.g., refraction) during sphere tracing by computing a local offset $\varepsilon_{\text{dynamic}}$ at each intersection point, rather than using a global constant [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of the provided evidence. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly describe 'Dynamic epsilon' as a method to prevent self-intersection artifacts in secondary rays (specifically mentioning refraction) during sphere tracing. They confirm that this method computes a local offset ($ε_{dynamic}$) at each intersection point using the formula $2 * max(ε_{min}, |f(p)|)$, rather than relying on a global constant, which is deemed inappropriate due to large variations in intersection distances.
